newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius MMM party quits ruling coalition.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius MMM party quits ruling coalition.

text.p: The Mauritian Militant Movement, the second largest party on the Indian Ocean island, has quit the government and gone into opposition, its leader Paul Berenger said.
Berenger told a news conference late on Friday the 25 MMM MPs and junior ministers would be dismissed from Saturday and would form the opposition at the next national assembly sitting on Monday.
It was not immediately clear what effect the move would have on the island's government.
Berenger said he would lead the opposition.
Mauritius President Cassam Uteem revoked Berenger's appointment as deputy prime minister and minister for Foreign Affairs, International and Regional Cooperation following the announcement.
Uteem, acting on the advice of prime minister Navin Ramgoolam, named Ramgoolam to the foreign affairs post, according to a statement on Saturday.
Berenger, who said he had long been exasperated with what he regarded as Ramgoolam's immobility on major socio-economic issues, met the prime minister for 90 minutes on Friday evening.
"Ramgoolam told me that he is revoking me as minister as from tonight (Friday) as he believes that the MMM was plotting to discredit him as prime minister..," Berenger said.
"In these circumstances, the MMM is expecting that all its ministers and junior ministers will leave the government in a gesture of solidarity with their leader," Berenger added.

The MMM-Labour Party won December 1995 general elections with a 100 percent sweep of all 60 national assembly seats, defeating Aneerood Juganauth's MSM alliance which had ruled for 13 years. Ramgoolam's Labour Party gained 35 seats with 25 going to MMM.
